Header.CaseTitle: Beacon Manufacturing Ltd v Alliance Insurance Plc

Counsel.Lead: Robert Anderson KC; Elizabeth Roberts (instructed by Hogan Lovells LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant seeks an indemnity under a business interruption insurance policy for losses suffered as a result of a fire at its manufacturing premises, contending that the Respondent has wrongfully declined the claim.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant held a combined commercial policy with the Respondent providing cover for material damage and business interruption.
A fire occurred at the Appellant's premises on 3 August 2023 causing extensive damage.
The Appellant submitted a claim for £4.2 million comprising property damage and 18 months' business interruption losses.
The Respondent declined the claim alleging non-disclosure of previous fires and breach of fire safety warranty.
The previous incidents were minor, did not result in claims, and were not material to the risk.

Contentions.item: The previous incidents were minor and not material to a prudent underwriter.
Any non-disclosure was not deliberate or reckless within the meaning of the Insurance Act 2015.
The warranty was suspended during the maintenance period under implied terms.
The Respondent's remedy is limited to proportionate reduction of the claim, not avoidance.

ReliefSought.item: Indemnity under the policy in the sum of £4,200,000

AuthoritiesCited.Authority: Versloot Dredging BV v HDI Gerling Industrie Versicherung AG [2016] UKSC 45
Brit Syndicates Ltd v Italaudit SpA [2008] UKHL 18

SourceExtracts.Quote: The Alliance Insurance Plc failed to discharge its duty of care in the circumstances.
The learned judge erred in concluding that the burden of proof had been satisfied.
The evidence before the court clearly established the breach alleged.
